meta.description: Style LoRA on FLUX.2 Klein 9B (gated on HF - accept the licence). VRAM: the 9B is ~29 GB in fp16 and ~15 GB at fp8, so a single 24 GB card (3090/4090/A5000) with quantization on is the published recommendation - the old "~32-48 GB" claim in this description was wrong. Network raised 2026-09-11 to BFL's OWN Klein style example - 128/64 linear + 64/32 conv (ratio 4:2:2:1), the full-scale recipe LDS also ships - replacing the half-scale 64/32 + 32/16 fold this preset inherited from the 4B. The halving was justified by "128 is too heavy for a 4B"; that argument never applied to the 9B and the model author publishes 128/64/64/32. BFL's style example also runs LR 9.5e-5 with weight decay 1.5e-4 over 3000 steps against the 1e-4 / 2500 shipped here - both are within the published spread, and a 50+-run community sweep independently found style runs preferring weight decay 1e-5, so treat LR and decay as the knobs to try, not rank. Weighted timesteps remain the one value with no published Klein source. Effective batch 1: raise to 4 only at >=40 files (advisor names the ceiling for your set). Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, machine-independent - the same table ships on every klein preset, laptop or desktop): 17 images ~1020, 20 images ~1200, 30 images ~1800, 40 images ~2400, 42 images ~2500, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 2500 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~42 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 2500 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Source: BFL's Klein training docs (start at 1500 steps for 20-50 images; LoRAs peak at 1000-1750) with the fork's 60 steps/image rule; community Klein 9B LoKr runs report near-full likeness at 1000-1500 steps on 20 images (r/StableDiffusion). Klein keeps its own 2500 plateau - below the 3000 general cap - because that is the published Klein ceiling. Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
